newsitem.title: CANADA: ATS shares jump on hefty supply deal.
newsitem.headline: ATS shares jump on hefty supply deal.

text.p: Shares in ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc soared by more than 20 percent after news of a hefty supply deal for a company, rumored to be Intel Corp, that would nearly double its 1996 revenues.
Stock in the automated systems and precision components maker soared 6.40 to 36.40 in brisk afternoon trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It earlier reached a 52-week high of 38.
The company refused to disclose its partner in the potentially lucrative contract, but analysts said it was rumored to be Intel.
ATS disclosed only that it was awarded the contract by a Fortune 500 microelectronics manufacturing company.

The contract to provide precision parts and some automated manufacturing systems, for an initial two years with an option for a third year, would be worth about US$375 million in revenue, said ATS Chief Financial Officer Ron Jutras.
ATS had revenues of C$250 million in the year ended March 31.

"If you've got a ... potential contract that's twice the size of the sales in the last fiscal year, that's obviously very good," said David Tyerman, Loewen Ondaatje McCutcheon's special situations analyst.
"There's been a lot of rumors about it being Intel, or somebody like that," Tyerman said.
Marko Pencak, Sprott Securities analyst, added: "that speculation is been out there for over a month."
Intel officals were not available to comment.

ATS, based in Cambridge, Ontario, started in automotive parts but is shifting to electronic components, Tyerman said. "They very much want to get into the electronics area in a larger way, and this will increase their penetration into that market," Tyerman said.
